method: Rank8/16/32 surrogate on train only, inspect JVPs, full kernel wall.

literature_checks.claim: DeepPCR casts a sequence of neural operations as an equation system solved by Parallel Cyclic Reduction, reducing cost from O(L) to O(log L) and reporting up to ~30x forward / ~200x backward MLP speedups.
literature_checks.transfer_caveat: Parallel reduction requires an exploitable operator system; there is no pretrained looped-Transformer KV benchmark.

literature_checks.claim: The authors solve nonlinear ODEs as a root-finding problem via Newton's method and parallelize the linearized recursion with parallel scans, claiming logarithmic span and runtime gains over Parareal.
literature_checks.transfer_caveat: General ODE dynamics lack attention-KV semantics, and the linearized operator cost may dominate on a GPU decoder.

reason: Deprioritised (not NO-GO) on measured prerequisite evidence: C3 directional probe on Huginn D32 BF16 gives median relative error 0.82 even for the best per-row scalar Jacobian surrogate (identity 1.04; response/delta cosine low), and Ouro gain 0.2 with alpha*~0.01. A rank-r JVP scan needs >= r extra core evaluations per depth per token to estimate the operator, which already exceeds the serial D-call budget at the batch sizes where width is not free (G1_WIDTH: Huginn T_F(32)/T_F(1) = 5.5x at B16, 15x at B64). Re-open if a cheap accurate operator surrogate appears.
